classification.difficultyReason: Combine fractions within both levels, divide and cancel common factors, while retaining exclusions from both inner denominators and a zero divisor.

answer.worked:
Combine each pair of fractions before dividing.
$$\begin{align*}\dfrac{\dfrac1{x-2}+\dfrac1{x-5}}{\dfrac1{x-1}+\dfrac1{x-6}}&=\dfrac{2x-7}{(x-2)(x-5)}\div\dfrac{2x-7}{(x-1)(x-6)}\\\dfrac{\dfrac1{x-2}+\dfrac1{x-5}}{\dfrac1{x-1}+\dfrac1{x-6}}&=\dfrac{2x-7}{(x-2)(x-5)}\times\dfrac{(x-1)(x-6)}{2x-7}\\\dfrac{\dfrac1{x-2}+\dfrac1{x-5}}{\dfrac1{x-1}+\dfrac1{x-6}}&=\dfrac{(x-1)(x-6)}{(x-2)(x-5)}.\end{align*}$$
The original denominators require $x\ne1,2,5,6$. The divisor must be nonzero, so $x\ne\dfrac72$.
